senses.gloss:
Ambarīṣa is mentioned as a Vārṣāgira in the Rigveda^1 along
with Ṛjrāśva, Sahadeva, Surādhas, and Bhayamāna.
1) i. 100, 17. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 140.

Āmba denotes in the Taittirīya^1 and Kāṭhaka^2 Saṃhitās a
grain, called Nāmba in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa^3
1) i. 8, 10, 1.
2) xv. 5.
3) v. 3, 3, 8.

Āmbaṣṭhya is mentioned in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (viii. 21)
as a king, whose priest for the Rājasūya, or royal inauguration,
was Nārada. Presumably the name is local, meaning ‘King of
[]
the Ambaṣṭhas,’ as interpreted in the St. Petersburg Dictionary.
Later the term Ambaṣṭha denotes ‘a man of mingled Brāhmaṇa
and Vaiśya parentage by father and mother’ respectively.
